brief:
Five Emirati aid convoys entered the Gaza Strip in a single week, carrying 75 trucks loaded with 663 tonnes of food and shelter material, the newspaper Emarat Al Youm reported on 9 August from the operation the Emirates calls Chivalrous Knight 3.

The trucks do not appear from nowhere. They are received, sorted and prepared at a logistics centre in El-Arish in Egypt before dispatch, an arrangement that has turned the supply into a weekly rhythm rather than a campaign that ends when the cameras leave.

Alongside the convoys the Emirati field hospital inside the Strip is running at 200 beds, and received a United Nations delegation in July that reviewed its work.

This is delivery, and it deserves to be stated precisely: goods that crossed a crossing, a patient who reached an operating room, not a promise in a closing communiqué.

The distance between what is delivered and what is pledged remains the larger story on the Arab support file. The big commitments directed at the World Bank-administered Gaza fund have not yet turned into transfers, on the fund's own reporting, while the convoys are counted in tonnes week by week.

The gap is not only an accounting question. Flour, a tent and a hospital bed arrive now; rebuilding a house, a school and a power station waits on the pledged money reaching the account.

title: The Emirates sent 75 aid trucks into Gaza in one week
